description: Path-length bias check for the revised Eq. (9) (reviewer R1-6: the summed path score favours higher-scoring, i.e. longer, paths). The revision defines Score(P) as the hop-averaged sum; this run re-derives the top-1 path for all 200 queries under the previous sum-only aggregation (path_score_normalize = true/false in pipeline config) and compares downstream metrics.
conclusion: Hop-averaging changes the top-1 reasoning path for 9/200 queries (paths of different lengths whose per-hop quality ordering differs from the summed ordering); all metric means shift by <= 0.004 and no significance conclusion changes. The two aggregations agree because the candidate path set is dominated by short paths (median 3 hops): length alone does not inflate the summed score of the surviving, circuit-breaker-filtered candidates. The manuscript now reports the hop-averaged definition and discloses this sensitivity check.
